subject: spanish
title: Wider Family
meta_desc: KS3 Spanish: grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins.
final_note: More family vocab for your whole tree.

walkthroughs.body_html: El tio = uncle. La tia = aunt. Notice how -o changes to -a for female versions.
El primo = male cousin. La prima = female cousin. The pattern -o (m) and -a (f) is everywhere in Spanish nouns.

mcqs.q: Which preposition expresses purpose ('in order to')?
How do you write 'Christmas' and 'Easter' in Spanish?
options: Navidad y Pascua (note: Semana Santa for Holy Week traditions).

mcqs.q: Why does 'qué' have an accent in '¿Qué quieres?' but not always elsewhere?
options: The accent distinguishes interrogative/exclamative 'qué' from relative 'que'.
